items.title: Mixed Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia as the Initial Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Mixed autoimmune hemolytic anemia (mAIHA) is a rare subtype of autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) characterized by the coexistence of warm (immunoglobulin G (IgG)) and cold (immunoglobulin M (IgM)) autoantibodies. It may occur as a primary disorder or secondary to underlying conditions, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We report the case of a 16-year-old female who presented with severe hemolytic anemia as the initial manifestation of SLE. On admission, her hemoglobin was 34 g/L with marked reticulocytosis and a positive direct antiglobulin test (DAT) demonstrating both IgG and IgM antibodies, confirming mAIHA. Immunological investigations revealed positive antinuclear antibody (ANA), anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibody, and anti-Smith antibody, supporting a diagnosis of SLE. At the time of the first presentation, she had no other clinical features suggestive of SLE. She was treated with blood transfusions and corticosteroids, resulting in significant improvement, and was discharged on a tapering prednisolone regimen. Shortly after, she was readmitted with a malar rash, arthralgia, joint swelling, nephrotic-range proteinuria, and worsening renal function. She was subsequently diagnosed with SLE complicated by lupus nephritis and recurrent AIHA. Following the rheumatology and nephrology review, she received intravenous methylprednisolone and was transferred to a tertiary care center for renal biopsy and further management. Renal biopsy demonstrated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). Further treatment with prednisolone, mycophenolate mofetil, intravenous belimumab, and hydroxychloroquine resulted in an excellent clinical response, with follow-up confirming remission. This case highlights mAIHA as a rare initial presentation of SLE and underscores the importance of early recognition, close monitoring, and multidisciplinary management, as patients presenting with AIHA may be at increased risk of developing lupus nephritis and other severe SLE-related complications.

items.title: Evaluation of a CT-like Multi-Echo 3D Gradient-Echo MR Sequence (FRACTURE) for Structural Assessment of the Sacroiliac Joints in Spondyloarthritis: Comparison with CT and T1-Weighted MR Imaging.
items.abstract: CT remains the imaging reference standard for evaluating structural sacroiliac joint (SIJ) lesions in spondyloarthropathy (SpA), but its use is limited by ionizing radiation. This retrospective single-center study evaluated a CT-like multi-echo 3D gradient-echo MRI sequence (FRACTURE) for structural SIJ assessment by comparing it with CT and conventional T1-weighted MR imaging (T1-WI). Consecutive adults who underwent SIJ MRI between November 2023 and October 2024 were included. Four radiologists assessed inflammatory sclerosis, erosions, and joint space changes using a structural severity score (SSS) derived from the SIMACT study and assigned a three-point Likert score for SpA diagnosis. Forty-three patients (median age, 49 years), including 22 with SpA, were analyzed. The area under the ROC curve for diagnostic Likert scores was 0.842 for T1-WI, 0.792 for CT, and 0.767 for FRACTURE (all pairwise comparisons, p > 0.05). Considering only definite diagnoses (Likert = 2), diagnostic accuracy reached 81.4% for CT, 76.7% for T1-WI, and 69.8% for FRACTURE, with 100% specificity for all three techniques. FRACTURE detected additional lumbosacral neojoints and accessory articular facets compared with T1-WI and showed a stronger correlation with CT for structural severity assessment (ρ = 0.814 vs. ρ = 0.774). Intra- and inter-observer reproducibility were good (all ICCs > 0.700). In conclusion, FRACTURE provides CT-like structural information with good reproducibility and showed a numerically higher correlation with CT for overall structural severity than T1-WI, while also improving the depiction of certain osseous anatomical variants relevant to differential diagnosis. However, it did not improve diagnostic performance for SpA diagnosis and showed lower performance for erosion assessment. FRACTURE may therefore provide complementary added value within MRI-based SIJ assessment, although further prospective validation is warranted.

items.title: Genetic Polymorphisms in Rheumatoid Arthritis: From GWAS-Identified Loci to Functional, Biomarker, and Pharmacogenomic Insights.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with a complex, multifactorial aetiology, in which both environmental factors and genetic predisposition play a significant role. This narrative review summarises the genetic polymorphisms associated with RA that have been identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Its aim is to synthesise the loci and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) reported to date, to relate them to the immunological mechanisms through which they are thought to act, and to assess their emerging diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacogenomic applications. Its scope covers large-scale GWAS and multi-ancestry meta-analyses together with the candidate-gene, functional, and pharmacogenomic studies required for their interpretation. Three principal conclusions emerge from the literature reviewed. First, the genetic architecture of RA remains dominated by the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, which is associated primarily with seropositive, anti-citrullinated protein antibody-positive disease, whereas the numerous non-HLA loci identified to date each confer only a modest individual effect. Second, these non-HLA variants converge on a limited number of biological processes-the activation thresholds of T and B lymphocytes, NF-κB and JAK-STAT cytokine signalling, and the invasive behaviour of fibroblast-like synoviocytes-so that their value lies less in the prediction of risk by individual variants than in identifying pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting. Third, the most readily translatable findings are pharmacogenomic. Variants affecting adenosine signalling and nucleotide metabolism modulate the response to methotrexate. Several polymorphisms predict the response to TNFα inhibitors. Polygenic risk scores are beginning to support the differential diagnosis of early inflammatory arthritis. Progress remains constrained by the over-representation of European-ancestry cohorts, by the difficulty of moving from an associated locus to a causal variant and its target gene, and by the limited replication of pharmacogenomic associations. Integration of genomic with transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, supported by machine learning approaches, is therefore required before genotype-guided management of RA can enter routine clinical practice.

items.title: Pulmonary Dysfunction Contributes to Nocturnal Hypoxemia Beyond Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severity in Primary Sjögren Syndrome.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Pulmonary involvement is a common extraglandular manifestation of primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) and may impair pulmonary gas exchange. Although obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been reported in pSS, the relationship between nocturnal hypoxemia and pulmonary dysfunction remains unclear. We investigated whether nocturnal oxygenation abnormalities in pSS are associated with pulmonary functional impairment beyond OSA severity. Methods : In this controlled cross-sectional study, 44 patients with pSS and 88 controls underwent overnight polysomnography. Pulmonary function testing, including diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO), and thoracic computed tomography were available for all pSS patients. Associations between nocturnal hypoxemia parameters and pulmonary function indices were assessed using correlation analyses. Predictors of minimum nocturnal oxygen saturation were evaluated using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, body mass index, and apnea-hypopnea index. Results : Sleep-disordered breathing severity and nocturnal oxygenation profiles were comparable between patients with pSS and controls, with the exception of a lower proportion of REM sleep in the pSS group. Within the pSS cohort, minimum nocturnal oxygen saturation correlated positively with DLCO, DLCO% predicted, DLCO/VA, and FVC% predicted. DLCO% predicted remained independently associated with minimum nocturnal oxygen saturation after adjustment for age, BMI, and AHI. However, this association was attenuated after additional adjustment for FVC, suggesting overlapping contributions of diffusion impairment and restrictive ventilatory dysfunction to nocturnal oxygenation. Conclusions : Although overall nocturnal oxygenation did not differ from that of matched controls, pulmonary functional impairment was associated with worse nocturnal oxygenation within the pSS cohort. These findings suggest that nocturnal hypoxemia in pSS reflects multiple interrelated aspects of pulmonary dysfunction rather than OSA severity alone. Assessment of pulmonary function, including both DLCO and FVC, may therefore provide clinically relevant information when evaluating nocturnal oxygenation abnormalities in patients with pSS.

items.title: Disease-Specific Clinical Correlates of Vitamin D in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Behçet's Disease.
items.abstract: Background and Objectives : Vitamin D deficiency is common in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and Behçet's disease (BD). However, whether it is associated with the same clinical parameters in both conditions remains unknown. Our objective is to compare the clinical correlates of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels in patients with SLE and BD. Materials and Methods : This exploratory cross-sectional study included 38 patients with SLE and 32 with BD. Spearman's correlation analyses, partial correlations controlling for sex, and tertile analyses were performed separately for each disease group. Results: Vitamin D deficiency [25(OH)D < 20 ng/mL] was similarly prevalent in SLE (64.9%) and BD (62.5%). However, distinct disease-specific correlation profiles were noted. In SLE, serum 25(OH)D levels were inversely correlated with body mass index (BMI) ( r = -0.47, p = 0.003) and parathyroid hormone (PTH) ( r = -0.40, p = 0.01), with no significant associations with inflammatory or haematological parameters. In patients with BD, 25(OH)D levels were positively correlated with haemoglobin ( r = 0.63, p < 0.001), haematocrit ( r = 0.58, p < 0.001), ferritin ( r = 0.47, p = 0.008), uric acid ( r = 0.48, p = 0.005), transferrin saturation ( r = 0.45, p = 0.02), and triglycerides ( r = 0.44, p = 0.01), while they were inversely correlated with total iron-binding capacity ( r = -0.50, p = 0.01) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) ( r = -0.44, p = 0.01). After adjusting for sex, the association between 25(OH)D and haemoglobin remained significant (partial r = 0.43, p = 0.01), as did the associations with haematocrit (partial r = 0.42, p = 0.02) and triglycerides (partial r = 0.43, p = 0.02). In contrast, the correlations with ferritin, ESR, uric acid, and transferrin saturation were attenuated and no longer statistically significant. Tertile analyses demonstrated dose-response relationships between vitamin D levels and BMI ( p = 0.01) and PTH ( p = 0.008) in SLE, and between vitamin D levels and haemoglobin ( p = 0.001) and ferritin ( p = 0.02) in BD. Conclusions : Despite the similar prevalence of vitamin D deficiency, patients with SLE and BD exhibit distinct vitamin D-associated clinical profiles. Vitamin D status was primarily associated with metabolic parameters in SLE and haematological parameters in BD. These disease-specific patterns may reflect differences in the underlying inflammatory pathways and pathophysiological mechanisms involved.

items.title: [Immunophenotype of RF - IgA - positive patients with primary Sjögren syndrome without concomitant rheumatoid arthritis: Dissociation between B - cell activation and inflammatory cytokine levels].
items.abstract: Primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by excessive B-cell activation. Rheumatoid factor (RF) is frequently positive in patients with pSS; however, the clinical significance of RF subtypes, particularly immunoglobulin (Ig) A rheumatoid factor (RF-IgA), remains unclear, and previous studies have often not strictly excluded patients with concomitant rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study aims to investigate the immunophenotypic characteristics of RF-IgA-positive patients with pSS without concomitant RA and to analyze the relationship between RF-IgA and disease activity. A total of 153 patients with pSS who presented to the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, between January 2021 and December 2025 were included, comprising 30 RF-IgA-positive patients and 123 RF-IgA-negative patients. Flow cytometry was used to determine the proportions of peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets, including CD19⁺ B cells, CD4⁺ T cells, CD8⁺ T cells, and CD16⁺CD56⁺ natural killer (NK) cells. Serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, IL-17A, interferon (IFN)-γ, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and IL-1β were measured using a cytometric bead array. Immunoglobulin and complement levels were measured by immunoturbidimetry. Anti-Sjögren syndrome-related antigen A (SSA)/60 kD, anti-SSA/52 kD, and anti-Sjögren syndrome-related antigen B (SSB)/La antibodies were detected by indirect immunofluorescence. Disease activity was assessed using the European League Against Rheumatism Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI), and the incidences of complications were compared between the 2 groups. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate the correlations of RF-IgA levels with the percentage of CD19⁺ B cells and serum IgA and IgG levels in the RF-IgA-positive group. The percentage of CD19⁺ B cells was significantly higher in the RF-IgA-positive group than in the RF-IgA-negative group, whereas the percentage of CD8⁺ T cells was significantly lower and the CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly higher in the RF-IgA-positive group (all P <0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in the percentages of CD4 + T cells or NK cells (both P >0.05). Serum IgA and IgG levels were significantly higher in the RF-IgA-positive group than in the RF-IgA-negative group (both P <0.05), whereas IgM levels did not differ significantly between the 2 groups ( P >0.05). The positive rates of anti-SSA/60 kD, anti-SSA/52 kD, and anti-SSB/La antibodies were significantly higher in the RF-IgA-positive group than in the RF-IgA-negative group (all P <0.05). There were no significant differences between the 2 groups in the levels of IL-6, IL-10, IL-17A, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-1β, complement 3 (C3), or complement 4 (C4) (all P >0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in ESSDAI scores or in the incidences of interstitial pneumonia, thyroid disease, chronic gastritis, or renal injury (all P >0.05). Spearman correlation analysis showed that RF-IgA levels were not significantly correlated with the percentage of CD19⁺ B cells ( r =0.106, P =0.557), but were positively correlated with serum IgA ( r =0.609, P <0.001) and IgG ( r =0.376, P =0.041) levels. RF-IgA-positive patients with pSS without concomitant RA exhibit immunological alterations characterized by an increased proportion of B cells, a decreased proportion of CD8⁺ T cells, an increased CD4/CD8 ratio, and elevated immunoglobulin levels and anti-SSA/SSB antibody positivity, suggesting enhanced B-cell activation and humoral immune responses. However, these alterations are not accompanied by significant changes in the measured inflammatory cytokines, complement levels, ESSDAI scores, or extraglandular involvement. RF-IgA positivity may identify a serological phenotype characterized by B-cell-related immune abnormalities; however, its clinical significance should be interpreted cautiously and should not be directly equated with increased disease activity. 目的 : 原发性干燥综合征(primary Sjögren syndrome，pSS)是一种以B细胞过度活化为特征的慢性自身免疫病，类风湿因子(rheumatoid factor，RF)在pSS中阳性率较高，但RF亚型的临床意义尚不明确，且既往研究多未严格排除合并类风湿关节炎(rheumatoid arthritis，RA)的患者。本研究旨在探讨RF-免疫球蛋白A(immunoglobulin A，IgA)阳性且不伴RA的pSS患者的免疫表型特征及其与疾病活动度的关系。 方法 : 纳入2021年1月至2025年12月于贵州中医药大学第二附属医院风湿免疫科就诊的153例pSS患者，其中RF-IgA阳性组30例，阴性组123例。采用流式细胞术检测外周血淋巴细胞亚群比例;流式细胞微球阵列法检测血清白细胞介素(interleukin，IL)-6、IL-10、IL-17A、干扰素(interferon，IFN)-γ、肿瘤坏死因子(tumor necrosis factor，TNF)-α及IL-1β水平;免疫比浊法检测免疫球蛋白及补体水平;间接免疫荧光法检测抗干燥综合征A型抗原(Sjögren syndrome-related antigen A，SSA)/60 kD、抗SSA/52 kD及抗干燥综合征B型抗原(Sjögren syndrome-related antigen B，SSB)/La抗体。采用欧洲抗风湿病联盟干燥综合征疾病活动指数(European League Against Rheumatism Sjögren’s Syndrome Disease Activity Index，ESSDAI)评估疾病活动度，比较2组间肺间质肺炎、淋巴瘤及甲状腺疾病等并发症发生率。采用Spearman相关分析评估RF-IgA阳性组中RF-IgA水平与分化簇(cluster of differentiation，CD)19⁺ B细胞百分比及血清IgA和IgG水平的相关性。 结果 : RF-IgA阳性组CD19⁺ B细胞比例高于阴性组，CD8⁺ T细胞比例低于阴性组，CD4/CD8比值高于阴性组(均 P< 0.05);2组CD4⁺ T细胞及自然杀伤(natural killer，NK)细胞比例差异均无统计学意义(均 P >0.05)。RF-IgA阳性组IgA及IgG水平均高于阴性组(均 P <0.05)，2组IgM水平差异无统计学意义( P >0.05)。RF-IgA阳性组抗SSA/60 kD、抗SSA/52 kD及抗SSB/La抗体阳性率均高于阴性组(均 P< 0.05)。2组间6种细胞因子、补体C3和C4水平的差异均无统计学意义(均 P >0.05)。2组ESSDAI及并发症肺间质肺炎、甲状腺疾病、慢性胃炎、肾损伤发生率的差异均无统计学意义(均 P >0.05)。Spearman相关分析显示，RF-IgA水平与IgA( r =0.609， P <0.001)及IgG( r =0.376， P =0.041)呈正相关，与CD19⁺ B细胞比例的相关性无统计学意义( r =0.106， P =0.557)。 结论 : 不伴RA的RF-IgA阳性pSS患者存在B细胞扩增、CD8⁺ T细胞减少、CD4/CD8比值升高、免疫球蛋白及抗SSA/SSB抗体水平升高等免疫学改变，提示B细胞活化和体液免疫增强。然而，该免疫活化表型未伴随炎症细胞因子水平的升高、补体水平的下降、ESSDAI的升高或腺外脏器受累的增加。RF-IgA阳性可标记一种以B细胞相关免疫指标改变为特征的血清学表型，该表型未伴随全身性炎症指标升高或疾病活动度增加，RF-IgA阳性的临床意义应审慎解读，不宜直接等同于疾病活动度升高。.

items.title: Familial Mediterranean Fever.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is the most common monogenic autoinflammatory disease, characterized by recurrent, self-limited inflammatory attacks beginning in childhood. Pathogenic variants in the MEFV gene lead to dysregulation of the pyrin inflammasome, excessive interleukin-1β production, and a persistently lowered inflammatory threshold. Although traditionally considered autosomal recessive, FMF demonstrates complex inheritance with clear genotype-phenotype correlations, particularly for high-penetrance mutations such as M694V. Genetic diagnosis confirms the diagnosis. Colchicine is the cornerstone of therapy and prevents Amiloid A (AA) amyloidosis, while interleukin-1 inhibitors offer effective alternatives in colchicine-resistant or intolerant patients.

items.title: A CCL20 + macrophage subpopulation is the major producer of TNF in axial spondyloarthritis synovium and is driven by CD40L and a myeloid autocrine circuit.
items.abstract: Tumour necrosis factor (TNF) and interleukin (IL)-17 are central drivers of axial spondyloarthritis (AxSpA). We previously identified activated CD4+ tissue-resident memory Th17 cells as the principal source of IL-17A/F in AxSpA synovium. We sought to define the cellular source of TNF and mechanisms driving the CCL20 + myeloid phenotype in joint and blood. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of synovial tissue from 5 patients with AxSpA was combined with immunofluorescence, synovial-fluid scRNA-seq, and flow cytometry, as well as comparisons with rheumatoid arthritis datasets. Monocyte-derived macrophages from healthy controls (HCs) and patients with AxSpA were cocultured with activated autologous CD4 + T cells, with blocking and cytokine experiments defining mechanisms of CCL20 + induction. Circulating monocytes were assessed by scRNA-seq and functional assays. CCL20 + macrophages were the predominant source of TNF in AxSpA synovium, with TNF protein confirmed in tissue and synovial fluid. Activated CD4 + T cells induced the CCL20 + phenotype through CD40L-CD40 signalling and an IL-1β/TNF-α autocrine circuit in HC-derived and AxSpA-derived cells. Baseline AxSpA monocytes showed a higher CCL20 + signature than HC monocytes, but this difference largely disappeared after T-cell-mediated induction. Under stimulation, AxSpA monocytes also produced more TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-23 than HC monocytes, a difference attenuated following IL-1/TNF priming. CCL20 + macrophages are a major CD40L- and IL-1β/TNF-α-driven source of TNF in AxSpA synovium. AxSpA circulating monocytes exhibit heightened basal CCL20 + signatures and inflammatory responsiveness that converge towards HC responses after inflammatory priming, supporting circulating CCL20 + monocytes as a marker of IL-1β/TNF-α-driven myeloid inflammation.

items.title: Predictors of treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: a narrative review.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common autoimmune disease having diverse responses to disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Although treat-to-target strategies have improved disease management, therapeutic selection remains largely empirical and a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve adequate clinical response to their therapies. Therefore, reliable biomarkers capable of predicting treatment response before therapy initiation are urgently needed to guide personalised treatment decisions. Current evidence suggests that multiple categories of biomarkers may contribute to the prediction of treatment responses across different therapeutic agents in RA, including clinical characteristics, serological markers, cytokine profiles, genetic and transcriptomic signatures, immune-cell phenotypes, synovial pathotypes and microbiome features. This review summarises current biomarker strategies for predicting therapeutic response in RA and discusses their potential utility in improving precision medicine. However, most individual biomarkers show limited predictive power, partly due to the complex and dynamic nature of RA pathogenesis. Combining biomarkers from multiple biological dimensions, together with the continued exploration of novel predictive markers, may improve the robustness and accuracy of treatment response prediction in RA.

items.title: Assessment of App Quality, User Experience, and Willingness to Recommend a Digital Therapeutic for Patients With Axial Spondyloarthritis: Subanalysis of a 12-Week Pretest-Posttest Intervention Study.
items.abstract: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease affecting the axial skeleton that requires regular physical exercise in addition to pharmacotherapy. However, a significant proportion of patients do not exercise frequently enough. Axia is a digital therapeutic (DTx) that offers a solution by providing a disease-specific and patient-tailored home-based exercise program for patients with axSpA. The app combines structured exercise with patient education and disease management features and incorporates gamification and behavioral conditioning to promote user engagement. However, it has remained unclear how Axia is perceived and evaluated by patients. This study aimed to describe app quality, user experience, and willingness to recommend the app to others after 12 weeks of use by applying standardized questionnaires. This single-center study was conducted at an outpatient tertiary clinic. After 12 weeks of ad libitum app use, 27 participants with axSpA completed paper-based assessments of the user version of the Mobile App Rating Scale (uMARS; range 1-5) and the net promoter score (NPS; range -100% to +100%). The mean overall uMARS app quality score was 4.44 (SD 0.43). Functionality received the highest mean score (4.54, SD 0.53), whereas information received the lowest (4.34, SD 0.49). The mean NPS was 9.52 (SD 0.75), corresponding to an overall NPS of 93%. The uMARS overall quality score correlated strongly with the NPS (ρ=0.57; P=.002). Except for physical therapy at baseline, no other baseline characteristic or therapeutic effect correlated with either the uMARS or NPS. Axia was perceived as a user-friendly DTx after 12 weeks of use. The findings support the acceptability of disease-specific DTx for patients with axSpA and the potential integration of DTx into routine care.

items.title: Interleukin-6 Blockade in Refractory Neuro-Behçet's Disease: A Systematic Literature Review.
items.abstract: This review aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of interleukin (IL)-6 inhibition in neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) refractory to standard immunosuppressive therapy. This systematic literature review was performed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. The PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science databases were searched for studies on the efficacy of IL-6 blockade in patients with refractory NBD. We also identified cases of NBD with recurrently elevated IL-6 levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) during tumor necrosis factor (TNF) alpha therapy at our institution. We identified 11 studies including 25 patients with NBD who were treated with tocilizumab. No eligible studies of other IL-6-targeted agents were identified. Among the 24 patients evaluated for response, 22 (91.7%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 74.2-97.7%) were classified as responders. Reduction of the glucocorticoid dose was achieved in at least 75.0% (18/24, 95% CI 55.1-88.0%) of patients receiving concomitant glucocorticoid. Adverse events were infrequently reported (infusion reaction, cytopenia, infections), and one responder experienced worsening mucocutaneous inflammation. Two cases identified at our institution had recurrent neurological symptoms with high CSF IL-6 levels and an incomplete response to TNF inhibitor therapy, requiring repeated hospitalization. IL-6 blockade is a promising option for patients with refractory or recurrent NBD who have failed conventional therapies. Given the limited quality of the current evidence, prospective studies are needed to clarify the long-term efficacy and safety of IL-6-targeted therapy in NBD. UMIN000058445.

items.title: Safety profiles of tocilizumab and tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis: a propensity score-weighted comparative analysis.
items.abstract: Biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) and targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) have been the primary advanced treatment options for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in Taiwan since 2010. Tocilizumab is an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor (IL-6Ri), whereas tofacitinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi). The two medications have similar mechanisms and efficacy. We compared the safety outcomes of tocilizumab and tofacitinib in patients with RA in real-world clinical settings. Patients with RA at any period between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database and followed until 2020. Propensity score stabilized weighting was used to balance the baseline characteristics of the tocilizumab and tofacitinib groups. The incidences of safety outcomes, specifically all-cause mortality, cancer, coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, overall venous thromboembolism (OVT), tuberculosis (TB), joint replacement events, and herpes zoster infection, were compared between the study groups. A total of 1074 patients with RA who were administered tocilizumab (n = 463) or tofacitinib (n = 611) were included in this study. The mean follow-up duration was 1.96 years in the tocilizumab group and 1.98 years in the tofacitinib group. A substantially lower incidence rate of herpes zoster infection (per 100 patient-years) was observed in the tocilizumab group (3.125) than in the tofacitinib group (6.875), with a hazard ratio of 0.455 (95% CI = 0.289-0.716; P = 0.0007). All-cause mortality, CHD, stroke, total hip replacement, and TB infection were similar between the two medication groups. Although tocilizumab (an IL-6 receptor inhibitor) and tofacitinib (a JAK inhibitor) effectively modulate the immune response through distinct mechanisms, a lower herpes zoster incidence rate was observed in the tocilizumab group. No statistically significant differences were detected for the other evaluated safety outcomes and mortality rates between the two groups, although the relatively small number of events resulted in wide confidence intervals. Key Points • For moderate to severe RA patients concerned about herpes zoster risk, the tocilizumab group had a lower incidence rate than the tofacitinib group. • In real-world settings, RA patients with tocilizumab or tofacitinib had comparable incidence rates of other safety concerns and mortality.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Phase-Contrast MR Angiography at 5 T Assesses Warming-Associated Changes in the Visible Hand Vascular Network in Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Thermal challenge can reveal vascular abnormalities in systemic sclerosis (SSc), but current assessments primarily measure surface temperature or cutaneous perfusion. Warming-associated changes in the visible three-dimensional hand vascular network in SSc remain incompletely characterized. To quantify warming-associated changes and group differences in hand-size-normalized metrics of visible hand vessels using 5-T three-dimensional phase-contrast MR angiography (3D PC-MRA), and to assess repeatability and reader agreement. Prospective case-control study. Ninety participants (60 SSc, mean age: 44.00 ± 10.73 years, 55 females; 30 healthy controls, mean age: 42.83 ± 13.24 years old, 28 females). Twenty controls (18 females) underwent baseline scan-rescan imaging; reader agreement was assessed in the 60 baseline examinations. 5 T; noncontrast-enhanced 3D gradient-echo PC-MRA. Hands were imaged before and after 5-min immersion in 40°C water. Hand-size-normalized metrics were vessel volume (nVol), centerline length (nLen), and apparent vessel radius (nRad); changes (Δ) were post-immersion minus baseline. Paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Welch t-tests; multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and baseline values; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs); and Bland-Altman analysis. Significance was q < 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction and p < 0.05 otherwise. Normalized vessel volume and normalized centerline length increased significantly in both groups, with mean changes of 0.76 × 10 -3 and 1.91 in controls and 1.80 × 10 -3 and 4.80 in SSc, respectively. Adjusted increases were significantly greater in SSc for normalized vessel volume (between-group difference, 1.11 × 10 -3 ; 95% CI, [0.36-1.85] × 10 -3 ) and normalized centerline length (difference, 1.97; 95% CI, 0.36-3.59). Changes in normalized apparent vessel radius did not differ after adjustment (difference, -0.001 × 10 -3 ; q = 0.996). Scan-rescan and reader-agreement ICCs were 0.948-0.994 and 0.941-0.993, respectively. At 5 T, 3D PC-MRA detected greater warming-associated increases in nVol and nLen in SSc than controls. Baseline measurements showed good-to-excellent scan-rescan repeatability in controls and excellent reader agreement. Stage 3. Systemic sclerosis can damage blood vessels and impair circulation in the hands. Researchers used noninvasive phase‐contrast magnetic resonance angiography to examine hand blood vessels before and after warm water immersion in patients and healthy volunteers. The analysis accounts for differences in hand size between participants. Warming increased visible vessel volume and length in both groups, with larger changes in patients. These changes reflect vessel visibility on images rather than new vessel formation. Repeated scans in healthy volunteers and repeated image readings produced consistent measurements. The findings support the feasibility of this approach for studying hand vascular responses in systemic sclerosis.

items.title: Genetic evidence linking gout to increased risk of epilepsy: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: While observational studies have explored the association between gout, uric acid (UA) levels, and the risk of epilepsy, their findings remain inconsistent. To clarify the potential causal relationship, we performed a Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. We conducted a bidirectional MR analysis using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary data. Epilepsy data were sourced from the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), gout data from the FinnGen consortium and a GWAS of clinically defined gout and its subtypes, and UA data from the BioBank Japan (BBJ) and a genome-wide meta-analysis of serum UA levels in Japanese individuals. The inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method served as the primary causal inference approach. To ensure robustness, we complemented this with 3 additional methods: MR-Egger, weighted median, and MR using Robust Adjusted Profile Score (MR-RAPS) - the latter specifically employed to account for potential weak instrument bias due to the limited number of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) included in this analysis. Our analysis identified a causal association between genetically predicted gout and an increased risk of epilepsy (odds ratio (OR) = 1.014, 95% confidence interval (95% CI): 1.011-1.017, p < 0.001), generalized epilepsy (OR = 1.009, 95% CI: 1.000-1.018, p = 0.042), and focal epilepsy (OR = 1.044, 95% CI: 1.002-1.088, p = 0.041) in Europeans. In contrast, UA levels showed no significant association with epilepsy or its subtypes in this population. Similarly, neither gout nor UA levels were linked to epilepsy in East Asians. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the robustness of the primary findings. This MR study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal role of gout in increasing the risk of epilepsy, including generalized and focal epilepsy, in European populations. In contrast, genetically predicted UA levels showed no significant association with epilepsy. These findings support a potential role of gout in epilepsy risk and warrant further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

items.title: Bilateral Earlobe Purpura as an Unusual Initial Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by autoantibody production, particularly antinuclear antibodies (ANAs). The broad clinical spectrum and absence of pathognomonic features can make diagnosis challenging, particularly when alternative autoimmune, infectious, and hematological conditions must be considered. We report a case of a 31-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of bilateral earlobe purpura. Initial investigations demonstrated severe thrombocytopenia and normocytic anemia, and subsequent imaging revealed widespread lymphadenopathy. Early multidisciplinary assessment by acute medicine, hematology, and rheumatology, together with exclusion of hematological malignancy and positive autoimmune serology, supported a diagnosis of SLE. Despite initial treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) and corticosteroids, the bicytopenia persisted. Mycophenolate mofetil was commenced; however, worsening cytopenias and concern for secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis led to the initiation of rituximab infusions. Her platelet count subsequently improved, and she was discharged with rheumatology and hematology follow-up. This case highlights an unusual cutaneous presentation of newly diagnosed SLE and the diagnostic challenges associated with severe hematological involvement at initial presentation. It also demonstrates the importance of multidisciplinary assessment and timely escalation of immunosuppressive therapy in severe disease.

items.title: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis mimicking seronegative rheumatoid arthritis: a case report of destructive erosive arthritis with partial response to Upadacitinib.
items.abstract: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis (MRH) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis that can mimic seronegative rheumatoid arthritis through destructive inflammatory arthritis and papulonodular skin lesions. We report a 44-year-old woman with progressive polyarthritis, purplish papulonodular lesions and destructive erosive disease of the hands and feet. Rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and antinuclear antibody were negative. Radiographs showed sharply demarcated erosions with prominent distal interphalangeal involvement, and skin biopsy confirmed MRH. Available malignancy screening, including oncology review, mammography, cervical screening and blood tests, was reassuring, although planned PET-CT was not completed due to loss to follow-up. Methotrexate and corticosteroids were not tolerated, certolizumab produced partial response, and upadacitinib led to modest cutaneous improvement but persistent active synovitis at four months. This case highlights MRH as a diagnostic mimic of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and illustrates discordant treatment response to JAK inhibition.

items.title: Patient-Reported Disease Activity, Health-Related Quality of Life, and Coping in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Online Survey in Switzerland (Lupus-IMPACT).
items.abstract: The impact of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) on the quality of life is differently perceived by patients and physicians. This survey explored the patient perception of SLE burden, challenges, and strategies of coping. Adults with a self-reported physician-diagnosis of SLE, living in Switzerland, were recruited to participate in a cross-sectional online survey through a patient association, a physician-confirmed national SLE registry, and a digital campaign. Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) was assessed using the Lupus Patient-Reported Outcome scale (LupusPRO ® ), disease activity using the Systemic Lupus Activity Questionnaire (SLAQ), and coping using the Brief Coping Orientation to Problems Experienced (COPE) inventory, in addition to a patient satisfaction questionnaire. Between February and June 2024, 146 participants completed the survey. Participants had a median age of 48.5 years (IQR 25), and 85.6% were female. Nearly all participants (92.5%) were receiving pharmacological treatments, with a median of six medications taken daily. In the preceding three months, patients reported mild (36.3%), moderate (21.9%), and severe (6.8%) flares. Participants reported impaired HRQoL, with especially affected domains of emotional health, cognition, pain and fatigue. Predominant coping domains were problem-focused in 106 participants (72.6%), emotion-focused in 25 (17.1%), avoidant-focused in 11 (7.5%), tied problem-/emotion-focused in 2 (1.4%), and tied problem-/avoidant-focused in 2 (1.4%). Fatigue reduction was the treatment goal most often reported by participants. In this cross-sectional Swiss survey, patients with SLE reported impaired HRQoL, frequent recent flares, and fatigue reduction as the most common treatment priority despite ongoing therapy. Problem-focused coping was the predominant coping style. These findings underscore the value of patient-reported outcomes in complementing clinical assessment and capturing patient-important disease burden. However, potential selection, non-response, confounding, and diagnostic uncertainties limit generalisability, and the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about causality or intervention benefit. Systemic lupus erythematosus, often called lupus, is a long-term autoimmune disease that can affect many parts of the body and can have a major impact on daily life. This study asked adults with lupus living in Switzerland about their symptoms, quality of life, coping strategies, treatment satisfaction, and treatment goals. In total, 146 participants completed an online survey between February and June 2024. Many participants reported recent disease flares, and overall quality of life was reduced, especially in relation to emotional health, cognition, pain, and fatigue. Although most participants were receiving treatment for lupus, reduction of fatigue remained the treatment goal most often reported as important. Most participants used problem-focused coping strategies, such as active coping and planning, to manage the challenges of living with lupus. These findings show that patient-reported outcomes can provide important information about aspects of lupus that matter most to patients and may not always be fully captured during routine medical consultations.

items.title: The Burden and Temporal Trends of Rheumatoid Arthritis in High-Income Countries and Territories, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease causing progressive joint damage, disability, and excess mortality. Evaluating long-term epidemiological trajectories across high-resource health systems is essential for optimizing rheumatology care. This study analyzes the burden and 33-year temporal trends of RA across high-income countries and territories using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2023 estimates. We analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 36 high-income countries and territories (5 GBD regions: Australasia, High-income Asia Pacific, High-income North America, Southern Latin America, and Western Europe) from 1990 to 2023. To distinguish clinical risk from population growth and aging, we prioritized age-standardized rates (ASRs per 100,000) alongside absolute metrics. We present all estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). In 2023, high-income settings accounted for 0.26 million incident cases, 4.98 million prevalent cases, 0.80 million DALYs, and 10,190 deaths. From 1990 to 2023, absolute prevalent cases (+72%) and DALYs (+49%) grew substantially due to demographic aging. Conversely, underlying age-standardized incidence (17.12 [95% UI: 15.69-18.83]) and prevalence (282.80 [95% UI: 256.24-314.48]) increased modestly (+9% and +10%), while age-standardized DALY rates (44.14 [95% UI: 32.63-56.59]) fell by 7% and age-standardized death rates (0.39 [95% UI: 0.34-0.45]) decreased markedly by 41%. Australasia exhibited the highest ASRs across all metrics in 2023, whereas Southern Latin America demonstrated the sharpest ASR increases (+54% incidence, +62% prevalence, +34% DALYs). High-income Asia Pacific achieved the largest ASR reductions (-14% incidence, -12% prevalence, -26% DALYs, -49% deaths). Females and adults aged over 60 years consistently bore the primary disease burden. While age-standardized mortality has dropped substantially, reflecting improved management of RA and its comorbidities, the non-fatal disability burden continues to expand alongside population aging. Rheumatology health services must shift toward long-term disability management, early treat-to-target intervention, and addressing persistent regional disparities.

items.title: [ Jiawei Qingluo Yin alleviates rheumatoid arthritis in rats by inhibiting activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway to promote apoptosis of synovial cells].
items.abstract: To investigate the mechanism of Jiawei Qingluo Yin (JWQLY) for alleviating rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in rats. Network pharmacology, molecular docking and dynamics analyses were performed to identify the core components, key targets, and pathways of JWQLY against RA and the core component-key target binding. In a rat model of antigen-induced arthritis (AIA) established using complete Freund's adjuvant, the effects of MTX (0.5 mg/kg) and low-, medium-, and high-dose JWQLY (1.03, 3.1, and 9.3 g/kg, respectively) were tested on paw swelling, arthritis index (AI), synovial histopathology, apoptosis, and serum IL-1β and VEGF levels. In the mechanistic investigation, the rat models were treated with high-dose (9.3 g/kg) JWQLY, vismodegib (a Hedgehog inhibitor, 10 mg/kg), or both, and the changes in paw swelling, AI, histopathology, and expressions of Bcl-2, Bax, Ihh, Smo, Gli1, cleaved caspase-3, and cleaved caspase-9 were examined. A total of 306 intersecting targets were identified between JWQLY and RA. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed enrichment of the targets in negative regulation of apoptosis and inflammation and in Hedgehog and apoptosis pathways. Molecular docking studies confirmed stable binding of the core components in JWQLY to Shh and other Hedgehog targets. The rat models of AIA showed obvious paw swelling and significantly elevated AI, pathology scores, and serum IL-1β and VEGF levels, and these changes were dose-dependently alleviated by JWQLY treatment. The rat models receiving treatment with vismodegib or JWQLY+ vismodegib exhibited significantly reduced Ihh, Smo, Gli1, and Bcl-2 expression with increased expressions of Bax, cleaved- caspase-3, and cleaved-caspase-9 and apoptosis rates of the synovial cells. JWQLY and vismodegib synergistically suppressed Hedgehog signaling and enhanced synovial cell apoptosis. JWQLY alleviates RA in rats by inhibiting Hedgehog pathway activation, down-regulating the Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and promoting synovial cell apoptosis. 目的 : 基于网络药理学、分子对接、分子动力学模拟与动物实验相结合的多技术融合策略探究加味清络饮（JWQLY）调控Hedgehog信号通路促进滑膜细胞凋亡治疗类风湿性关节炎（RA）的作用机制研究。 方法 : 通过网络药理学分析确定JWQLY治疗RA的核心成分、关键靶点及信号通路，采用分子对接和分子动力学模拟对核心成分与关键靶点的结合活性进行验证。采用完全弗氏佐剂诱导建立AIA大鼠模型，在疗效观察阶段，将造模成功的大鼠随机分为正常组、模型组、甲氨蝶呤（MTX）（0.5 mg·kg -1 ·d -1 ）组、JWQLY低、中、高剂量（1.03、3.1、9.3 g·kg -1 ·d -1 ）组。观察大鼠一般生理指标、足爪肿胀度及关节炎指数（AI）评分;采用HE染色观察滑膜组织病理学变化;采用TUNEL法检测细胞凋亡;采用ELISA法检测血清白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）、血管内皮生长因子（VEGF）水平。在机制验证阶段，将造模成功的AIA大鼠模型随机分为正常组、模型组、JWQLY高（9.3 g·kg -1 ·d -1 ）组、抑制剂组（维莫德吉，10 mg·kg -1 ·d -1 ）及JWQLY+抑制剂组。观察大鼠一般生理指标、足爪肿胀度及关节炎指数（AI）评分;采用HE染色观察滑膜组织病理学变化;采用免疫组化法检测滑膜组织Bcl-2、Bax蛋白表达;采用Western blotting法检测滑膜组织Ihh、Smo、Gli1、cleaved-caspase-3、cleaved-caspase-9蛋白表达。 结果 : 通过网络药理学筛选JWQLY靶点518个、RA疾病靶点4210个，交集靶点306个。GO富集分析显示靶点主要涉及凋亡过程的负调控、炎症反应等生物过程;KEGG通路富集分析显示靶点显著富集于Hedgehog信号通路以及凋亡信号通路。分子对接及分子动力学模拟结果表明，核心成分与Hedgehog通路关键靶点Shh等具有稳定的结合活性。疗效观察阶段结果显示，与正常组比较，模型组大鼠足爪肿胀明显，AI评分、病理评分、血清IL-1β及VEGF水平显著升高（ P <0.05），且呈剂量依赖性。机制验证阶段结果显示，与模型组比较，抑制剂组和JWQLY+抑制剂组滑膜组织Ihh、Smo、Gli1、Bcl-2蛋白表达显著降低（ P <0.05），Bax、cleaved-caspase-3、cleaved-caspase-9蛋白表达及细胞凋亡率显著升高（ P <0.05）;JWQLY与抑制剂联用后对Hedgehog通路产生协同抑制作用，进一步促进滑膜细胞凋亡。 结论 : JWQLY通过抑制Hedgehog信号通路激活，下调Bcl-2/Bax比值，促进滑膜细胞凋亡，进而缓解类风湿关节炎病变。.

items.title: Immunogenicity, Safety, and Clinical Outcomes Following Homologous and Heterologous SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination Regimens in Patients with Axial Spondyloarthritis and Psoriatic Arthritis: A Prospective Observational Study from the SAFER Cohort.
items.abstract: Patients with spondyloarthritis (SpA) frequently receive immunomodulatory therapies that may influence vaccine-induced immune responses. However, evidence comparing the immunogenicity, safety, and clinical outcomes following homologous and heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination regimens in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) remains limited. This observational study was conducted within the Brazilian multicenter SAFER cohort and included adults with axSpA or PsA who received three doses of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines through the Brazilian National Immunization Program. The primary outcome was humoral immunogenicity, assessed by anti-receptor-binding domain (anti-RBD) IgG geometric mean titers (GMTs). Clinical outcomes, disease activity, and safety were evaluated throughout follow-up. Ninety patients (axSpA = 69; PsA = 21) were included. Antibody titers increased progressively after vaccination, with GMTs rising from 6.70 BAU/mL at baseline to 907.72 BAU/mL after the additional dose. Humoral responses were comparable between axSpA and PsA throughout follow-up. Participants with previous SARS-CoV-2 exposure consistently exhibited higher antibody responses than infection-naïve individuals. Although ChAdOx1-S elicited stronger early humoral responses than CoronaVac, heterologous regimens incorporating a BNT162b2 additional dose produced the highest post-additional-dose antibody concentrations. Serological response rates reached 100% after the additional dose, irrespective of disease subtype or vaccination regimen. Biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), including TNF inhibitors, were not significantly associated with reduced antibody responses. Only four COVID-19 cases occurred during follow-up, with no hospitalizations or deaths. Disease activity remained stable, and adverse events were predominantly mild and self-limited. SARS-CoV-2 vaccination was safe and highly immunogenic in patients with axSpA and PsA, without compromising disease activity control. Heterologous vaccination regimens incorporating a BNT162b2 additional dose elicited the strongest humoral immune responses. These findings provide prospective real-world evidence supporting optimized additional-dose strategies and may inform future vaccination approaches for patients with SpA.

items.title: AI-Guided Histopathological and Molecular Phenotyping of Salivary Glands in Sjögren's Disease: Subtyping, Mechanistic Insights, and Translational Implications-A Systematic Review and Structured Functional Synthesis.
items.abstract: Salivary-gland biopsy is central to Sjögren's disease (SjD) assessment, but conventional measures incompletely capture glandular heterogeneity. This systematic review evaluated artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) applications to SjD salivary-gland histopathology and molecular profiling, including biological and translational validation. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched. Eligible studies used salivary-gland tissue as the primary analytical substrate or provided substantive glandular validation of systemic AI/ML findings. Evidence was synthesized functionally because of methodological heterogeneity. Twenty-five studies were included. AI/ML identified histopathological and molecular phenotypes spanning immune/interferon activation, tissue architecture and immune-cell organization, epithelial stress and metabolic/cell-death remodeling, and translational response. Only a limited subset progressed beyond computational or tissue-level confirmation to functional perturbation, pharmacological testing, in vivo validation, or human treatment-response assessment. Recurrent public-dataset reuse, small cohorts, heterogeneous pipelines, and limited independent validation constrained reproducibility. AI/ML supports multidimensional SjD glandular phenotyping and shows emerging translational potential, but demonstrated clinical or therapeutic utility remains unestablished. Prospective multicenter validation is required before AI-derived glandular phenotypes can inform routine patient stratification or therapeutic decision-making.

items.title: Chromosomal Radiosensitivity in Sjögren's Syndrome with and Without Concomitant Malignancy.
items.abstract: Connective tissue diseases have long been hypothesized to confer increased radiosensitivity and radiotherapy-related toxicity, although findings vary between disease entities. In a previous institutional study, we found increased radiosensitivity in patients suffering from systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), primarily in patients with concomitant malignancy. We therefore investigated Sjögren's syndrome, an autoimmune disease for which evidence has been limited. Ex vivo chromosomal radiosensitivity was assessed in 45 patients with Sjögren's syndrome (27 non-oncological, 18 oncological) by three-color fluorescence in situ hybridization after 2 Gy irradiation of G0 peripheral blood lymphocytes. Results were compared with 211 healthy controls, 129 breast cancer patients, and the previously characterized SLE cohorts (37 non-oncological, 33 oncological). Demographic, clinical, serological, and treatment-related associations were explored in 31 deeply phenotyped patients. Radiosensitivity was significantly increased in non-oncological Sjögren patients (0.527 breaks per metaphase (B/M)) compared with healthy controls (0.411 B/M; p < 0.001) and non-oncological SLE patients (0.404 B/M; p = 0.001), and it remained similarly elevated in oncological Sjögren patients (0.527 B/M), whereas in SLE increased radiosensitivity was predominantly associated with concomitant malignancy. High-grade anti-SSB positivity was associated with increased radiosensitivity in the unadjusted analysis ( p = 0.016), but did not withstand correction for multiple testing ( q = 0.124). Sjögren's syndrome is associated with increased ex vivo chromosomal radiosensitivity, with no further apparent increase in patients with concomitant malignancy. This pattern differs from SLE and may suggest a stronger contribution of disease-associated factors. High-grade anti-SSB positivity may represent a relevant serological signal in relation to radiosensitivity, but requires validation in larger cohorts. These findings support closer consideration of individual radiosensitivity in Sjögren's syndrome and highlight the need for prospective studies integrating ex vivo radiosensitivity with radiotherapy-related toxicity and treatment outcomes in this patient population.

items.title: Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease in Systemic Sclerosis: A Scoping Review of the Literature.
items.abstract: Background : Patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc) may be affected by pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD), a poorly characterized form of group I pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). This scoping review aimed to systematically map the literature regarding SSc-PVOD to identify key clinical features, knowledge gaps, and future research areas. Methods : A systematic literature search was conducted (January 1970 to May 2026) across PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We included adult patients with right heart catheterization (RHC)-confirmed SSc-PAH and a concurrent/subsequent diagnosis of PVOD established via pulmonary edema following vasodilators, highly suggestive chest HRCT findings, or histopathology. Results : A total of 20 articles were included, encompassing 63 SSc-PVOD patients (87.2% females). Chest HRCT revealed ≥2 highly suggestive abnormalities (centrilobular ground-glass opacities, interlobular septal thickening, mediastinal lymphadenopathy) in 46/54 patients. Almost all patients had mPAP > 35 mmHg at diagnosis, and 12/25 had DLCO < 30%. Lung tissue was obtained in 13 patients (11 post-mortem); predominant histological findings were venous luminal narrowing (11/13), arteriole fibrosis (9/13), and thickened interalveolar septae (9/13). Notably, 20 out of 24 patients treated with pulmonary vasodilators developed pulmonary edema. Overall, two patients underwent lung transplantation, and 33 (52%) died. Conclusions : SSc-PVOD mimics classic SSc-PAH at RHC but carries a high risk of PAH-treatment-induced pulmonary edema. Early non-invasive recognition is vital to avoid drug-related harm and prompt transplant referral. Novel anti-remodeling therapies should be explored.

items.title: Associations of Physical Activity, Sedentary Behavior, and Handgrip Strength with Clinical Characteristics in Women with Rheumatoid Arthritis from Western Mexico.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that affects synovial joints and leads to functional impairment. Modifiable factors such as physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and handgrip strength (HGS) may influence clinical and functional outcomes; however, these relationships have been insufficiently studied in Mexican women with RA. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the associations of PA, SB, and HGS, with clinical characteristics in women with RA from western Mexico. PA and SB were assessed using the short form of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ-S). Disability was evaluated using the Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index (HAQ-DI), HGS was measured by dynamometry, and disease activity was assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP). Inflammatory and serological markers (CRP, RF, anti-CCP, and ESR) were determined using standard analytical methods. The study included 58 women with RA, with a mean DAS28-CRP score of 3.25 ± 1.16. PA was inversely associated with CRP levels (β = -0.312, p = 0.023), with higher CRP concentrations observed among patients with low PA levels. SB was positively associated with HAQ-DI scores (β = 0.345, p = 0.008) and DAS28-CRP scores (β = 0.420, p = 0.001). HGS was inversely associated with DAS28-CRP (β = -0.323, p = 0.04) and HAQ-DI (β = -0.521, p = 0.0004), independent of age and body mass index. In conclusion, lower PA levels were associated with higher CRP concentrations, whereas lower HGS and greater SB were associated with greater disease activity and disability in women with RA.

items.title: Antibody Discovery and Therapeutics in Spondyloarthritis: Recent Advances and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Spondyloarthritis is a multi-faceted condition housing a group of inter-related chronic inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as ankylosing spondylitis, IBD-associated arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. While decades of research and technological advancements have significantly improved our understanding of the disease, there remain many underlying genetic and physiological mechanisms which are unsolved but essential for the development of the right diagnosis and treatment. This mini-review examines our current foundational knowledge of spondyloarthritis, the main concepts related to the disease pathogenesis and the various lines of therapies developed thus far. We hope to provide a perspective on the current and potential antibody discovery platforms for the next decade as computational methods and artificial intelligence become increasingly mature and relevant in clinical research.

items.title: Association of Airway Disease and Single-Nucleotide Variants in PTPN14 and IL9RP3 in Japanese Cases of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Objectives: Airway disease, commonly related to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), confers an inferior prognosis. Few genetic analyses in RA have investigated patient susceptibility to airway disease. We examined if single-nucleotide variants related to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis susceptibility were related to airway disease in Japanese cases of RA. Methods: Genotyping for rs4233306 [C/T] in PTPN14 and rs3930589 [T/C] in IL9RP3 in 246 patients with RA and airway disease, and 425 with RA but without chronic lung disease was performed. Results: PTPN14 rs4233306C and IL9RP3 rs3930589T were significantly related to airway disease in RA under a dominant model for minor alleles ( p = 0.0398; odds ratio [OR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.96; p = 0.0462; OR 3.19; 95% CI 1.06-9.63, respectively). Stratification by male sex resulted in the remaining significant association of PTPN14 rs4233306 with airway disease in RA cases ( p = 0.0028; OR 3.70; 95% CI 1.55-8.84). A significant relationship between IL9RP3 rs3930589 and airway disease in RA patients aged > 65 years was noted ( p = 0.0135; OR 9.79; 95% CI 1.21-79.20). Conclusions: This is the first study to report associations of rs4233306 and rs3930589 with airway disease in Japanese RA cases.

items.title: Superb microvascular imaging versus CT angiography for assessing disease activity in pediatric Takayasu arteritis: a comparative study with high consistency.
items.abstract: To compare the value and consistency of superb microvascular imaging (SMI) and CT angiography (CTA) for assessing disease activity in pediatric Takayasu arteritis (TA), and to explore the feasibility of SMI as a non-invasive screening tool. Forty-seven children with TA treated at our hospital between May 2019 and January 2025 were included. Disease activity was determined using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) criteria, and patients were classified into active (n = 26) and inactive (n = 21) groups. All patients underwent both SMI and CTA. The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of SMI grading and CTA for diagnosing TA activity were analyzed. Kappa tests were used to assess consistency with NIH criteria. Inter-observer agreement for SMI grading was also evaluated. SMI grading was significantly higher in the active group than in the inactive group (Z = 5.388, p < 0.001). Using SMI grade ≥ II as the cutoff, SMI had a sensitivity of 84.62%, specificity of 95.24%, and accuracy of 89.36%. CTA had a sensitivity of 88.46%, specificity of 90.48%, and accuracy of 89.36%. The AUC values were 0.885 for SMI and 0.895 for CTA. SMI showed good consistency with NIH criteria (Kappa = 0.788), as did CTA (Kappa = 0.786). Inter-observer agreement for SMI grading was good (Kappa = 0.865, 95% CI: 0.777-0.953), with 43 of 47 cases (91.49%) showing complete concordance. SMI and CTA demonstrate comparable diagnostic performance and high consistency in assessing disease activity in pediatric TA. Given its non-invasive nature, absence of radiation, no need for contrast agents, and repeatability, SMI is recommended as the preferred screening tool for long-term follow-up of disease activity in pediatric TA, with CTA reserved for cases where SMI suggests activity or when precise vascular assessment is needed.

items.title: The shared burden of frailty in rheumatoid arthritis - a qualitative study of informal caregiving roles and support needs from the perspectives of patients and their informal caregivers.
items.abstract: Frailty is increasingly recognized among older patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and is associated with functional decline and growing dependence on others. As frailty progresses, significant others often assume extensive practical, emotional, and coordinative responsibilities, becoming informal caregivers. Given that RA is commonly managed across healthcare sectors, these responsibilities may also involve navigating and coordinating care across settings. Yet, their experiences and support needs remain underexplored in rheumatology care. This study aimed to explore how frailty in older patients with RA affects their informal caregivers, including the support they provide and their perceived needs, as understood by both older patients and informal caregivers themselves. Individual, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 17 older patients with RA and frailty (11 women, mean age 74) and thirteen informal caregivers (5 women, mean age 69). Older adults were recruited from four rheumatology outpatient clinics affiliated with Copenhagen University Hospital, Denmark. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Three interrelated themes were developed: (1) Gradual consolidation of caregiving in everyday life, (2) Emotional landscape of caregiving, and (3) Persistently navigating the healthcare system. Caregiving was identified as a progressively expanding role that reshaped daily routines, introduced emotional strain, and required navigation of fragmented healthcare services. Both patients and informal caregivers highlighted a need for clearer information about RA symptoms and disease trajectories, as well as care pathways and available support services, alongside improved coordination in the healthcare system and greater recognition of the roles of informal caregivers. The findings suggest that frailty in RA affects not only patients but also those closest to them. Recognizing informal caregivers as key partners in care and strengthening communication between health professionals across healthcare sectors may help mitigate caregiver burden.

items.title: Nonuniform settlement of C2 lateral mass: a pathological anatomic change related to the lateral atlantoaxial osteoarthritis.
items.abstract: Nonuniform settlement of C2 lateral mass (C2LM-NUS) was defined as an asymmetrical change of the bilateral C2 lateral masses. This study aimed to determine the association between the nonuniform settlement of C2 lateral mass (C2LM-NUS) and lateral atlantoaxial osteoarthritis (AAOA). A total of 573 patients who underwent a head and neck or cervical spine CT scan were reviewed. The morphological parameters were measured, including C2 lateral mass settlement (C2LMS), lateral atlantodental interval (LADI), coronal deviation angle of odontoid process (Od-CDA), and C1/2 relative rotation angle (C1/2 RRA). The lateral AAOA was recorded. The patients with a difference in C2LMS between the bilateral sides (d-C2LMS) of more than 1.4 mm were assigned to the C2LM-NUS group. There were 154 patients in the C2LM-NUS group and 419 in the control group. The median values of the difference in LADI between the two sides (d-LADI), Od-CDA, and C1/2 RRA in the C2LM-NUS group were greater than those in the control group (p < .001 for all). The prevalence of lateral AAOA in patients with C2LM-NUS was higher than in the control group (33.8% vs 19.1%, p < .001). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that the C2LM-NUS was an independent risk factor for lateral AAOA (Adjusted Odds Ratio: 2.382, p < .001). This study indicated that the C2LM-NUS, an independent anatomical risk factor for lateral AAOA, was associated with asymmetric morphological changes of the AAJ.

items.title: Clinical features and outcomes of nocardiosis in Thai patients with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Nocardiosis is a rare but life-threatening opportunistic infection in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), although data on childhood-onset SLE remain scarce. The objectives of this study were to determine the prevalence, clinical features, associated factors, and outcomes of nocardiosis in cSLE. A retrospective cohort study was conducted in a tertiary academic center including cSLE patients followed between January 2009 and August 2024. Culture-confirmed nocardiosis cases were identified through systematic review of electronic medical records. Firth penalized logistic regression was used to explore baseline factors associated with the development of nocardiosis. Seven out of 323 patients (2.2%) developed culture-confirmed nocardiosis. All were female with a mean age at diagnosis of 11.9 ± 3.1 years. The median (interquartile range) duration from cSLE diagnosis to nocardiosis diagnosis was 4.3 (2.1-13.4) months, with 71.4% occurring within the first year. All patients were receiving corticosteroids at a mean prednisolone-equivalent dose of 1.7 ± 1.3 mg/kg/day at the time of infection. The respiratory tract involvement manifesting as pneumonia was the most common infection site (71.4%). Proliferative lupus nephritis had an exploratory association with nocardiosis (OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.19-28.36, p = 0.028). Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis at initial SLE diagnosis was significantly more frequent in the nocardiosis group (28.6% vs. 4.4%, p = 0.014). Carbapenem-based induction followed by trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) consolidation was used in the majority of patients. The in-hospital mortality rate from the index nocardiosis episode was 0%, and the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%, attributable to secondary Corynebacterium septicemia in the patient with the most multiple immunosuppressive drug therapy with cumulative burden. Nocardiosis affects 2.2% of cSLE patients and occurs predominantly early in the disease course. Proliferative lupus nephritis had an exploratory association with nocardiosis, highlighting the need for heightened clinical vigilance and the use of antimicrobial susceptibility testing to guide management in high-risk patients.
